ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, it is a structure in which a benzene ring is fused with a five-membered imide ring; there are two carbonyl oxygens on the five-membered ring, and the nitrogen atom in the ring is connected to an R substituent; in the upper right there is additionally a negatively charged OH/oxygen anion fragment, and multiple curved arrows are drawn. Then reason: the problem requires ignoring the arrows and recording only the connection relationships of atoms and bonds. The fused benzene ring-imide skeleton corresponds to N-substituted phthalimide, which can be written as *N1C(=O)c2ccccc2C1=O, where * represents the R/wildcard substituent on the nitrogen. The separate negative oxygen fragment in the upper right is transcribed as [O-] according to the specification, and it is not bonded to the main structure, so it is separated with a dot.

planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use skeletal-structure-to-SMILES rules: aromatic benzene atoms are lowercase c, carbonyls are C(=O), ring closures are numbered, disconnected species are separated by '.', a generic R substituent attached to nitrogen is represented by wildcard '*', and the separate negative oxygen is written as [O-].
